title: Six skills for startup success: what founders should build before starting
summary: Garry Tan lists six skills that raise a founder's odds: engineering, product, design, sales and marketing, finance, and management and leadership. Go deep in one or two, stay broad in the rest so you can hire and work with experts, and fill the gaps with a team. Skills make startup risk more calculated, not deterministic.

principles.text: Be deep in one or two core skills and broad enough in the rest to judge and work with experts.
principles.quote: Be deep in one or two of these areas but broad enough to be dangerous in the rest. You actually need this to be able to tell who's actually good in those positions and to be able to work with those best people in those expertise areas.

principles.text: More skills attract better cofounders and employees, since talent avoids projects that look likely to fail without them.
principles.quote: The more of these skills you have, the more you will attract high quality people to come work with you, whether it's cofounders or employees.

principles.text: Technology is the ultimate moat; non-technical founders should learn to build a good-but-imperfect version to stand out.
principles.quote: If you understand the craft and you can build a good but not perfect version of what you ultimately want to build, you can get the ball rolling.

principles.text: Product is a continuous process of finding and refining product-market fit; learn it by shipping and talking to users.
principles.quote: Build something and release it, release it to users and see if they stick with it.

principles.text: Interaction design is the core of design and ties directly to product; taste matters for every business now.
principles.quote: Interaction design is probably the meat of design when I think about it.

principles.text: Finance is not critical at the start but becomes essential from zero to one, to know whether you are growing or dying.
principles.quote: Finance and budgeting allows you to make sense of the decisions you have to make in a business.
